## The fix
In `pre_commit/git.py`'s `get_conflicted_files()`, the merge-diff command was passing the refnames `HEAD` and `MERGE_HEAD` bare:

```
git diff --name-only --no-ext-diff -z -m <tree> HEAD MERGE_HEAD
```

A tracked file named `HEAD` (or `MERGE_HEAD`) makes git read the token as both a revision and a path, so the command dies with `fatal: ambiguous argument 'HEAD': both revision and filename`. I added the `--` separator so the refnames are unambiguously revisions and there are no pathspecs:

```
'-m', tree_hash, 'HEAD', 'MERGE_HEAD', '--',
```

This keeps the full result set — the `MERGE_MSG` conflict filenames plus all merge-diff filenames (including a colliding file that actually changed) — and doesn't swallow the error or return an empty/partial set.

Added `test_get_conflicted_files_refname_collision`, parametrized over `HEAD` and `MERGE_HEAD`, to `tests/git_test.py` following the existing `in_merge_conflict`/`resolve_conflict` fixture style. It creates and stages a tracked file named after the ref and asserts the result is exactly `{'conflict_file', refname}` (the collision must still be reported, not silently dropped).
